name: NUCLEUS
summary: NUCLEUS develops gram-scale cryogenic calorimeters for coherent scattering of reactor antineutrinos at Chooz-B. Very low recoil thresholds are intended to compensate for its small target mass and open a low-energy weak-interaction test.
detection_principle: Cryogenic calcium-tungstate and sapphire crystals convert recoil energy into phonons measured with superconducting transition-edge sensors. Inner and outer veto systems and passive shielding suppress surface, cosmic and ambient-radioactivity backgrounds.

sites.name: France; Chooz nuclear power plant site
sites.location: France; Chooz nuclear power plant site

status.label: Commissioning
status.evidence: The collaboration reports a March 2026 empty-cryostat cooldown and April 2026 installation of the detector cage at Chooz; this is commissioning, not an established neutrino observation.

timeline.event: Shielding and veto transported to Chooz
Cryogenic system at Chooz reached 7 mK
Detector cage containing the target module and cryogenic outer veto installed at Chooz

collaboration.name: NUCLEUS Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Design recoil threshold
key_parameters.value: 10–20 eV; a design goal rather than a demonstrated CEvNS threshold

key_parameters.name: Chooz baselines
key_parameters.value: Approximately 72 and 102 m from the two cores

key_parameters.name: 2026 installed module
key_parameters.value: Four CaWO4 target crystals inside six high-purity-Ge veto crystals

results.summary: The TUM commissioning campaign validated stable operation and characterized backgrounds; no reactor-neutrino observation is asserted by that commissioning report.
